proofs.proof_tex:
Put
\[
 a_0=\frac{\min\{B,L,1\}}{64},\qquad
 \bar e=(e_1^{\top},0,\ldots,0)^{\top}\in\mathbb R^{Sd},
 \qquad q_0=(\bar e^{\top}\Sigma\bar e)^{1/2}.
\]
The positivity of \(B\) and \(L\) gives \(a_0>0\).  We first verify the covariance facts needed below.  From \texttt{def:worked-modulus-dgp},
\[
 \Sigma=\frac12I_{Sd}+\frac{1}{2Sd}\mathbf 1_{Sd}\mathbf 1_{Sd}^{\top}.
\]
The vector \(\mathbf 1_{Sd}\) is an eigenvector with eigenvalue one, while every vector orthogonal to it is an eigenvector with eigenvalue one half.  Thus \(\Sigma\) is positive definite, \(q_0>0\), and the restrictions \(c_\Sigma\le1/2\) and \(C_\Sigma\ge1\) in \texttt{def:worked-modulus-dgp} imply
\[
 c_\Sigma I_{Sd}\preceq\Sigma\preceq C_\Sigma I_{Sd}.
\]
This verifies \texttt{ass:donor-ellipticity}.  Every off-diagonal entry of \(\Sigma\) is \(1/(2Sd)>0\), so the claimed full-covariance nondegeneracy also holds.

We next verify the causal and support conditions.  At \(z_0=\tfrac12\mathbf 1_{Sd}\), both formulas for \(m_1\) in \texttt{def:worked-modulus-dgp} give \(m_1(z_{01})=4a_0\), and \(m_s(z_{0s})=4a_0\) for \(s>1\).  Hence
\[
 B_{si}(0)\in\{3a_0,5a_0\},
 \qquad B_{si}(1)=B_{si}(0)+a_0\in\{4a_0,6a_0\}.
\]
In particular, \(B_{si}(a)>0\) for \(a\in\{0,1\}\), and therefore \(R_{si0}(a)=B_{si}(a)-1>-1\).  By \texttt{def:buyhold-level} and the assignments \(W_{si,-1}=1\) and \(R_{sih}(a)=0\) for \(h>0\),
\[
 W_{si,-1}\prod_{h=0}^{H}\{1+R_{sih}(a)\}
 =1\cdot B_{si}(a)\prod_{h=1}^{H}1
 =B_{si}(a),
\]
where the last product is empty and equal to one when \(H=0\).  The prescribed equality \(B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}=B_{si}(1)\) is \texttt{ass:consistency}.  Because \(\eta_{si}\) is centered and independent of \(z_0\),
\[
 \mathbb E[B_{si}(0)\mid z_0]
 =m_s(z_{0s})+a_0\mathbb E[\eta_{si}\mid z_0]
 =m_s(z_{0s}),
\]
which is \texttt{ass:event-date-transport}.

For boundedness, when \(\kappa=1\), write \(y=x_1-1/2\).  Since \(-1/2\le y\le1/2\) and \(-1/4\le y+y^2\le3/4\),
\[
 \frac{15a_0}{4}\le m_1(x)\le\frac{19a_0}{4}.
\]
When \(0<\kappa<1\), the positive and negative parts in the formula for \(m_1\) cannot both be nonzero, and
\[
 \frac{7a_0}{2}\le m_1(x)\le5a_0.
\]
The remaining surfaces equal \(4a_0\).  Since all response noises take values in \(\{-1,1\}\), these bounds and the preceding event-outcome calculation yield
\[
 |Q_{sti}|\vee|B_{si}(0)|\vee|B_{si}(1)|
 \le6a_0
 \le\frac{6B}{64}<B.
\]
Thus \texttt{ass:bounded-wealth} holds.

It remains to verify \texttt{ass:holder-regression}.  If \(0<\lambda<1\), then \(\kappa=\lambda\).  The elementary inequality
\[
 |v_+^{\lambda}-w_+^{\lambda}|\le |v-w|^{\lambda}
\]
and its negative-part analogue show that the nonconstant part of \(m_1\) has \(\lambda\)-Holder seminorm at most \(a_0\) when two arguments are on the same side of \(x_1=1/2\).  If they are on opposite sides, each one-sided coordinate distance is at most the distance between the arguments, so the seminorm is at most \(3a_0/2\).  Consequently,
\[
 \|m_1\|_{\infty}+[m_1]_{\lambda}
 \le5a_0+\frac{3a_0}{2}<7a_0<L.
\]
If \(\lambda\ge1\), the selected surface is the quadratic surface, whose only possibly nonzero derivatives of positive order are
\[
 \partial_1m_1(x)=a_0\{1+2(x_1-1/2)\},
 \qquad \partial_{11}m_1(x)=2a_0.
\]
The first derivative is bounded by \(2a_0\) and is Lipschitz with constant \(2a_0\); the second derivative is bounded by \(2a_0\); and every derivative of order greater than two vanishes.  Under the stated integer-order convention, the usual isotropic Holder norm is therefore at most \(9a_0<L\) for every \(\lambda\ge1\).  Each constant surface has norm \(4a_0<L\).  This proves \texttt{ass:holder-regression}.  The selected first-cohort surface is non-affine because it has a nonzero quadratic term when \(\kappa=1\) and an asymmetric cusp when \(0<\kappa<1\).

The variables \(X_{st}\) are independent and uniform on \([0,1]^d\), so their common density is \(f_X(x)=1\).  Since \(c_X\le1\le C_X\), this is \texttt{ass:design-density}.  Moreover,
\[
 \operatorname{dist}(z_{0s},\partial[0,1]^d)=\frac12\ge\delta_0,
\]
which is \texttt{ass:interior-path}.  The product construction makes each cohort's calendar sequence independent across \(t\), although responses within a window share \(X_{st}\).  Hence its absolute-regularity coefficients satisfy
\[
 \beta(k)=0\le\beta_0\rho_0^k\qquad(k\ge1),
\]
verifying \texttt{ass:temporal-mixing}.

Let \(\mathcal X=\sigma((X_{uv})_{1\le u\le S,\,1\le v\le T})\).  Independence and centering of the response noises give, for every \(s,t,i\),
\[
 \mathbb E[Q_{sti}\mid z_0,\mathcal X]
 =m_s(X_{st})+a_0\mathbb E[\varepsilon_{sti}\mid z_0,\mathcal X]
 =m_s(X_{st})
\]
and
\[
 \mathbb E[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0,\mathcal X]
 =m_s(z_{0s})+a_0
 =\mathbb E[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0].
\]
These are the two equalities in \texttt{ass:design-conditional-centering}.  Conditional on \((z_0,\mathcal X)\), the independent arrays \((\varepsilon_{sti},\eta_{si})\) make the unit histories mutually independent across \((s,i)\), which is \texttt{ass:cross-unit-independence}.  The construction records each \(X_{st}\) itself as the training coordinate, proving \texttt{ass:center-only-design}.  The product-law independence of the donor Rademacher vectors from \(\mathcal X\), all response noises, and all event noises is \texttt{ass:donor-training-separation}.  The response law is nondegenerate because
\[
 \operatorname{Var}(Q_{sti}\mid z_0,\mathcal X)=a_0^2>0,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Var}(B_{si}(a)\mid z_0,\mathcal X)=a_0^2>0.
\]

Finally, the donor vectors \(U_j\) are independent and identically distributed with \(\mathbb E[U_j]=0\) and \(\operatorname{Var}(U_j)=I_{Sd}\).  Thus
\[
 \mathbb E[Z_j\mid z_0]=z_0,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Var}(Z_j\mid z_0)
 =\Sigma^{1/2}I_{Sd}\Sigma^{1/2}=\Sigma,
\]
which verifies \texttt{ass:donor-independence} and \texttt{ass:donor-unbiasedness}.  Also,
\[
 \mathbb E\!\left[\|\Sigma^{-1/2}(Z_j-z_0)\|_2^4\mid z_0\right]
 =\mathbb E[\|U_j\|_2^4]
 =(Sd)^2\le B^4,
\]
by the displayed restriction in \texttt{def:worked-modulus-dgp}; this is \texttt{ass:donor-fourth-moment}.  We have verified every member property in \texttt{def:panel-model-class}, and therefore
\[
 P_{\mathrm{ex}}\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}.
\]

It remains to derive the local modulus; no lower-modulus premise is used.  For \(0<\delta\le\delta_0\), define
\[
 u_\delta=\frac{\delta\Sigma\bar e}{q_0}.
\]
Since \(q_0^2=\bar e^{\top}\Sigma\bar e\),
\[
 \|\Sigma^{-1/2}u_\delta\|_2^2
 =\frac{\delta^2}{q_0^2}\bar e^{\top}\Sigma\bar e
 =\delta^2,
 \qquad
 \bar e^{\top}u_\delta
 =\delta q_0>0.
\]
The radius restriction in \texttt{def:worked-modulus-dgp} gives
\[
 \|u_\delta\|_\infty
 \le\delta_0\|\Sigma\bar e/q_0\|_\infty
 \le\frac12.
\]
Since \(z_0=\tfrac12\mathbf 1_{Sd}\), it follows that \(z_0+u_\delta\in([0,1]^d)^S\).  Thus \(u_\delta\) is feasible in \texttt{def:local-modulus}.

Only the first coordinate of the first cohort contributes to the weighted increment.  If \(\kappa=1\), the stacked weighted gradient at \(z_0\) is \(\pi_1a_0\bar e\), whose covariance-standardized dual norm is
\[
 \|\Sigma^{1/2}(\pi_1a_0\bar e)\|_2
 =\pi_1a_0q_0>0.
\]
Substituting \(u_\delta\) gives the exact increment
\[
 \sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s\{m_s(z_{0s}+u_{\delta,s})-m_s(z_{0s})\}
 =\pi_1a_0(q_0\delta+q_0^2\delta^2)
 =\frac{\pi_1\min\{B,L,1\}q_0}{64}\delta+O(\delta^2).
\]
It is in particular at least \(\pi_1a_0q_0\delta\).  If \(0<\kappa<1\), positivity of \(\bar e^{\top}u_\delta\) instead gives
\[
 \sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s\{m_s(z_{0s}+u_{\delta,s})-m_s(z_{0s})\}
 =\pi_1a_0q_0^\kappa\delta^\kappa
 =\frac{\pi_1\min\{B,L,1\}q_0^\kappa}{64}\delta^\kappa.
\]
Therefore \texttt{def:local-modulus} implies
\[
 \omega_{P_{\mathrm{ex}}}(\delta;z_0)
 \ge \pi_1a_0\min\{q_0,q_0^\kappa\}\delta^\kappa.
\]

For the reverse inequality, let \(u\) be any feasible perturbation in \texttt{def:local-modulus}.  The upper ellipticity bound gives
\[
 \|u\|_2
 =\|\Sigma^{1/2}\Sigma^{-1/2}u\|_2
 \le C_\Sigma^{1/2}\delta.
\]
Put \(v=\bar e^{\top}u\).  Feasibility of \(z_0+u\) implies \(|v|\le1/2\).  If \(\kappa=1\),
\[
 |m_1(z_{01}+u_1)-m_1(z_{01})|
 =a_0|v+v^2|
 \le\frac32a_0|v|
 \le\frac32a_0C_\Sigma^{1/2}\delta.
\]
If \(0<\kappa<1\), the two branches of the asymmetric cusp give
\[
 |m_1(z_{01}+u_1)-m_1(z_{01})|
 \le a_0|v|^\kappa
 \le a_0C_\Sigma^{\kappa/2}\delta^\kappa.
\]
Every other cohort surface is constant, and \(0<\pi_1\le1\).  Taking the supremum over feasible \(u\) yields a finite constant \(C_{\mathrm{ex}}>0\), depending only on fixed class parameters, such that
\[
 \omega_{P_{\mathrm{ex}}}(\delta;z_0)\le C_{\mathrm{ex}}\delta^\kappa
 \qquad(0<\delta\le\delta_0).
\]
Together with the preceding positive lower bound, this proves
\[
 \omega_{P_{\mathrm{ex}}}(\delta;z_0)\asymp\delta^\kappa
 \qquad\text{as }\delta\downarrow0.
\]
Thus this bounded, noisy member of the base Holder panel class has the asserted attainable full-covariance modulus, while the argument makes no such assertion for an arbitrary member of that class.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed: The law \(P_{\mathrm{ex}}\) in \texttt{def:worked-modulus-dgp} belongs to \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}\) for the displayed admissible constants and is nondegenerate: its responses have bounded nonzero conditional noise, its design point is interior, and its full stacked donor covariance is positive definite with nonzero off-diagonal entries. Let \(\bar e=(e_1^{\top},0,\ldots,0)^{\top}\in\mathbb R^{Sd}\). For every \(0<\delta\le\delta_0\), set \(u_\delta=\delta\Sigma\bar e/(\bar e^{\top}\Sigma\bar e)^{1/2}\). Then \(\|\Sigma^{-1/2}u_\delta\|_2=\delta\) and \(\bar e^{\top}u_\delta=\delta(\bar e^{\top}\Sigma\bar e)^{1/2}>0\). Consequently, when \(\kappa=1\), the weighted surface has nonzero standardized gradient and its increment along \(u_\delta\) is \(\pi_1\min\{B,L,1\}(\bar e^{\top}\Sigma\bar e)^{1/2}\delta/64+O(\delta^2)\); when \(0<\kappa<1\), the positive asymmetric-cusp increment is \(\pi_1\min\{B,L,1\}(\bar e^{\top}\Sigma\bar e)^{\kappa/2}\delta^{\kappa}/64\). Hence \(\omega_{P_{\mathrm{ex}}}(\delta;z_0)\asymp\delta^{\kappa}\) as \(\delta\downarrow0\). This construction establishes non-vacuity only and does not derive the lower modulus for the general panel class.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The current statement leaves delta unquantified and asserts a strict positive inner product, which is false at delta equal to zero. Restricting the displayed direction to the intended punctured local-modulus domain makes the boundary condition explicit without changing the substantive claim.

proposed.statement: The law \(P_{\mathrm{ex}}\) in \texttt{def:worked-modulus-dgp} belongs to \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}\) for the displayed admissible constants and is nondegenerate: its responses have bounded nonzero conditional noise, its design point is interior, and its full stacked donor covariance is positive definite with nonzero off-diagonal entries. Let \(\bar e=(e_1^{\top},0,\ldots,0)^{\top}\in\mathbb R^{Sd}\). For every \(0<\delta\le\delta_0\), set \(u_\delta=\delta\Sigma\bar e/(\bar e^{\top}\Sigma\bar e)^{1/2}\). Then \(\|\Sigma^{-1/2}u_\delta\|_2=\delta\) and \(\bar e^{\top}u_\delta=\delta(\bar e^{\top}\Sigma\bar e)^{1/2}>0\). Consequently, when \(\kappa=1\), the weighted surface has nonzero standardized gradient and its increment along \(u_\delta\) is \(\pi_1\min\{B,L,1\}(\bar e^{\top}\Sigma\bar e)^{1/2}\delta/64+O(\delta^2)\); when \(0<\kappa<1\), the positive asymmetric-cusp increment is \(\pi_1\min\{B,L,1\}(\bar e^{\top}\Sigma\bar e)^{\kappa/2}\delta^{\kappa}/64\). Hence \(\omega_{P_{\mathrm{ex}}}(\delta;z_0)\asymp\delta^{\kappa}\) as \(\delta\downarrow0\). This construction establishes non-vacuity only and does not derive the lower modulus for the general panel class.
proposed.justification: The explicit calculation shows that the maintained lower-modulus condition is compatible with bounded noisy panel laws and non-affine response surfaces.
proposed.gap: The general frontier assumes one attainable Mahalanobis direction; this proposition supplies a concrete nondegenerate member rather than claiming that Holder smoothness alone implies attainability.
proposed.consumer: Referees can audit the donor lower-bound channel on a legal bounded DGP before assessing the general conditional minimax proof.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The proposition derives the local modulus directly, so ass:attainable-local-modulus is a circular and obsolete dependency after its removal from the base model. The proof also uses def:buyhold-level to verify that the prescribed potential outcomes are the constructed buy-and-hold wealth levels.

proofs.proof_tex:
Let
\[
 \mathcal X=\sigma\!\left((X_{uv})_{1\le u\le S,\,1\le v\le T}\right),
 \qquad
 p_E=\Pr_P(E\mid z_0),
 \qquad
 \mu_{si}=\mathbb E_P[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0].
\]
The conditional mean exists by \texttt{ass:design-conditional-centering}.  Since \(E\in\mathcal X\), the random variable \(b\mathbf 1_E\) is measurable with respect to \(\sigma(z_0,\mathcal X)\).  The assumed equality \(B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}=b\mathbf 1_E\), valid almost surely under the conditional law given \(z_0\), therefore implies
\[
 \mathbb E_P[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0,\mathcal X]
 =b\mathbf 1_E
 \quad\text{almost surely under that conditional law}.                                      \tag{1}
\]
On the other hand, \texttt{ass:design-conditional-centering} gives
\[
 \mathbb E_P[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0,\mathcal X]
 =\mathbb E_P[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0]
 =\mu_{si}
 \quad\text{almost surely}.                                                                  \tag{2}
\]
Taking conditional expectation given \(z_0\) in the assumed shock representation gives
\[
 \mu_{si}=b\,\mathbb E_P[\mathbf 1_E\mid z_0]=bp_E.                                           \tag{3}
\]
Combining (1)--(3), squaring, and taking conditional expectation given \(z_0\) yields
\[
 0
 =\mathbb E_P[(b\mathbf 1_E-bp_E)^2\mid z_0]
 =b^2\mathbb E_P[(\mathbf 1_E-p_E)^2\mid z_0]
 =b^2p_E(1-p_E).                                                                              \tag{4}
\]
The last equality uses \(\mathbf 1_E^2=\mathbf 1_E\) and \(\mathbb E_P[\mathbf 1_E\mid z_0]=p_E\).  Because \(b\ne0\), division by \(b^2\) in (4) gives \(p_E(1-p_E)=0\).  Since every conditional probability lies in \([0,1]\), it follows that
\[
 \Pr_P(E\mid z_0)=p_E\in\{0,1\}.
\]

For the former scalar construction in the statement, \(z_0\) is fixed, \(X_{11}\sim\operatorname{Unif}[0,1]\), \(E=\{X_{11}\le q\}\), and \(q\in(0,1)\).  Hence
\[
 \Pr_P(E\mid z_0)=\Pr_P(X_{11}\le q\mid z_0)=q\in(0,1).
\]
Taking \(b=b_*>0\) contradicts (4).  Thus the shocked law violates \texttt{ass:design-conditional-centering}; by the member-property construction in \texttt{def:panel-model-class}, it is not an element of \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}\).  The former obstruction required the shocked law to belong to that class, so the obstruction is excluded.  Notice that this argument uses the observed-law centering condition, not causal event-date transport.

Fix \(P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}\), a cohort \(s\), and a unit \(i\), and put
\[
 \mu_{si}=\mathbb E_P[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0].
\]
This conditional mean is finite by \texttt{ass:bounded-wealth}.  By \texttt{ass:design-conditional-centering},
\[
 \mathbb E_P[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}-\mu_{si}\mid z_0,\mathcal X]=0.                            \tag{5}
\]
Let \(W\) be bounded and \(\mathcal X\)-measurable.  Then \((B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}-\mu_{si})W\) is integrable by boundedness, and \(W\) is measurable with respect to \(\sigma(z_0,\mathcal X)\).  The pull-out and tower properties of conditional expectation applied to (5) give
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \mathbb E_P[(B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}-\mu_{si})W\mid z_0]
 &=\mathbb E_P\!\left[
 W\,\mathbb E_P(B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}-\mu_{si}\mid z_0,\mathcal X)
 \mathrel{\Big|}z_0\right]\\
 &=0.
\end{aligned}                                                                                \tag{6}
\]
This is the claimed conditional orthogonality.

Now take \(E\in\mathcal X\) and write \(p_E=\Pr_P(E\mid z_0)\).  Substituting \(W=\mathbf 1_E\) into (6) gives
\[
 \mathbb E_P[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mathbf 1_E\mid z_0]=\mu_{si}p_E.                          \tag{7}
\]
If \(p_E>0\), division of (7) by \(p_E\), using the definition of conditional expectation on an event, yields
\[
 \mathbb E_P[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0,E]=\mu_{si}.                                     \tag{8}
\]
Applying the same argument to \(E^c\) gives
\[
 \mathbb E_P[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0,E^c]=\mu_{si}                                   \tag{9}
\]
whenever \(p_E<1\).  Thus (8)--(9) hold simultaneously if \(0<p_E<1\).  The exclusion of the former common-design-shock experiment is precisely \texttt{lem:common-design-shock-obstruction}.

It remains to prove that this centering repair does not itself fix the centered event-noise constant.  We give the two laws required by the statement for every positive \(N,T,n_1\).  Choose the following admissible scalar fixed parameters:
\[
 S=1,
 \quad \pi_1=1,
 \quad H=0,
 \quad p=d=1,
 \quad z_0=\frac12,
 \quad \lambda=\kappa=1,
 \quad B=L=1,
 \quad \delta_0=\frac14,
\]
and take \(c_X=C_X=c_\Sigma=C_\Sigma=1\), with arbitrary fixed \(\beta_0>0\) and \(\rho_0\in(0,1)\).  The identity \(d=p(H+1)=1\) is satisfied.  Define the untreated regression and training experiment by
\[
 m_1(x)=\frac12,
 \qquad
 X_{1t}\stackrel{\mathrm{iid}}{\sim}\operatorname{Unif}[0,1],
 \qquad
 Q_{1ti}=m_1(X_{1t})=\frac12
 \quad(1\le t\le T,\ 1\le i\le n_1).                                                       \tag{10}
\]
Let \(\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_N\) be independent Rademacher variables, independent of the entire training experiment, and set
\[
 Z_j=\frac12+\xi_j,
 \qquad 1\le j\le N.                                                                         \tag{11}
\]
For every event unit put \(W_{1i,-1}=1/2\) and \(R_{1i0}(0)=0\).  By \texttt{def:buyhold-level},
\[
 B_{1i}(0)=\frac12.                                                                           \tag{12}
\]
Under \(P^{(0)}\), set \(R_{1i0}(1)=0\).  Under \(P^{(1)}\), let \(\varepsilon_1,\ldots,\varepsilon_{n_1}\) be independent Rademacher variables, independent of the design and donor variables, and set \(R_{1i0}(1)=\varepsilon_i/2\).  In both laws impose \texttt{ass:consistency} by defining \(B_{1i}^{\mathrm{obs}}=B_{1i}(1)\).  The buy-and-hold formula then gives
\[
 B_{1i}^{\mathrm{obs}}
 =\frac12
 \quad\text{under }P^{(0)},
 \qquad
 B_{1i}^{\mathrm{obs}}
 =\frac12+\frac14\varepsilon_i
 \quad\text{under }P^{(1)}.                                                                  \tag{13}
\]
All constructed returns belong to \((-1,\infty)\), because their smallest possible value is \(-1/2\).

We next verify every defining condition of \(\mathcal M_{N,T,(n_1)}\).  Equations (10), (12), and (13) imply
\[
 |Q_{1ti}|=\frac12,
 \qquad
 |B_{1i}(0)|=\frac12,
 \qquad
 |B_{1i}(1)|\le\frac34,
\]
so \texttt{ass:bounded-wealth} holds with \(B=1\).  The constant \(m_1\) has supremum norm \(1/2\), every positive-order derivative equal to zero, and Holder seminorm zero.  Hence \(m_1\in\mathcal H_1(1,1)\), as required by \texttt{ass:holder-regression}.  Moreover,
\[
 \operatorname{dist}\!\left(\frac12,\partial[0,1]\right)=\frac12\ge\delta_0,
 \qquad
 f_X(x)=1\quad(0\le x\le1),                                                                  \tag{14}
\]
which verifies \texttt{ass:interior-path} and \texttt{ass:design-density} with the displayed \(c_X,C_X\).

Conditional on the complete design array, every training outcome in (10) is deterministic.  Under \(P^{(0)}\), the event outcomes are deterministic; under \(P^{(1)}\), the event history of unit \(i\) depends only on \(\varepsilon_i\).  Independence of the \(\varepsilon_i\)'s therefore proves \texttt{ass:cross-unit-independence}.  The calendar blocks in (10) are independent over \(t\), so their beta-mixing coefficients obey
\[
 \beta(k)=0\le\beta_0\rho_0^k,
 \qquad k\ge1,                                                                               \tag{15}
\]
which proves \texttt{ass:temporal-mixing}.  Declaring each \(X_{1t}\) in (10) directly observed verifies \texttt{ass:center-only-design}.

Let \(\mathcal X=\sigma((X_{1t})_{t=1}^{T})\).  Equation (10) gives
\[
 \mathbb E_P[Q_{1ti}\mid z_0,\mathcal X]
 =\frac12
 =m_1(X_{1t}).                                                                                \tag{16}
\]
Under either law, (13), independence of \(\varepsilon_i\) from \(\mathcal X\), and \(\mathbb E[\varepsilon_i]=0\) give
\[
 \mathbb E_P[B_{1i}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0,\mathcal X]
 =\frac12
 =\mathbb E_P[B_{1i}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0].                                               \tag{17}
\]
Thus both clauses of \texttt{ass:design-conditional-centering} hold.

By (11), conditional on the fixed \(z_0=1/2\), the donor scores are independent and identically distributed, are independent of the training and event samples, and satisfy
\[
 \mathbb E_P[Z_j\mid z_0]=z_0,
 \qquad
 \Sigma=\operatorname{Var}_P(Z_j\mid z_0)=1.                                                 \tag{18}
\]
Consequently \texttt{ass:donor-independence}, \texttt{ass:donor-training-separation}, and \texttt{ass:donor-unbiasedness} hold.  Since \(c_\Sigma=C_\Sigma=1\), (18) also proves \texttt{ass:donor-ellipticity}.  Finally,
\[
 \mathbb E_P\!\left[
 |\Sigma^{-1/2}(Z_j-z_0)|^4\mid z_0
 \right]
 =\mathbb E[|\xi_j|^4]
 =1
 =B^4,                                                                                        \tag{19}
\]
which verifies \texttt{ass:donor-fourth-moment} while retaining the full scalar covariance.

Equation (12) and the definition of \(m_1\) give
\[
 \mathbb E_P[B_{1i}(0)\mid z_0]
 =\frac12
 =m_1(z_0),                                                                                  \tag{20}
\]
so \texttt{ass:event-date-transport} holds.  Consistency was imposed before (13).  We have therefore verified every member property listed in \texttt{def:panel-model-class}, and hence \(P^{(0)},P^{(1)}\in\mathcal M_{N,T,(n_1)}\).  In particular, no lower local-modulus condition is used.

The joint law of \((X_{1t},Q_{1ti},Z_j)\) is the same under \(P^{(0)}\) and \(P^{(1)}\) by (10)--(11).  By \texttt{def:target}, (12)--(13), and the zero mean of a Rademacher variable,
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \tau_{P^{(0)}}(z_0)
 &=\mathbb E_{P^{(0)}}[B_{1i}(1)-B_{1i}(0)\mid z_0]=0,\\
 \tau_{P^{(1)}}(z_0)
 &=\mathbb E_{P^{(1)}}[B_{1i}(1)-B_{1i}(0)\mid z_0]
 =\frac14\mathbb E[\varepsilon_i]=0.
\end{aligned}                                                                                \tag{21}
\]
Nevertheless, (13) and independence of \(\varepsilon_i\) from \(\mathcal X\) yield
\[
